title: Neural combinatorial optimization with reinforcement learning in industrial engineering: a survey
justification: Survey (secondary study) focusing on neural combinatorial optimization with reinforcement learning; no mention of Digital Twins. Fails IC1 and is excluded by EC3.

title: Scaled non-passive environmental interaction force tracking for telerobotic manufacturing system with variable time delay
justification: The article focuses on telerobotic teleoperation control and force feedback stability in manufacturing and does not mention or discuss Digital Twins. Since Digital Twin is not a relevant or central concept (violating IC1), it clearly falls under EC1 (unrelated to Digital Twins). Although human interaction is present, the absence of any Digital Twin context makes it ineligible for Phase 1.

title: City-scale residential energy consumption prediction with a multimodal approach
justification: EC1: The article is clearly unrelated to Digital Twins. While it uses explainability methods (feature importance, partial dependence), there is no mention or context of Digital Twins, so IC1 is not satisfied.

title: Lightweight mechanical equipment fault diagnosis framework based on GCGAN-MDSCNN-ICA model
justification: The article presents a machine-learning-based fault diagnosis framework (GCGAN and MDSCNN-ICA-BiGRU) for mechanical equipment without any mention of Digital Twins or explainability/human interaction aspects. It clearly fails IC1 and meets EC1 as unrelated to Digital Twins.

title: Vehicle-to-Everything Communication in Intelligent Connected Vehicles: A Survey and Taxonomy
justification: EC1 and EC3: The article is a survey on V2X communication for intelligent connected vehicles and does not mention or focus on Digital Twins. It is also a secondary study (survey). No evidence of explainability or human-interaction aspects in a Digital Twin context.

title: Human-centered GeoAI foundation models: where GeoAI meets human dynamics
justification: EC1: The article focuses on GeoAI foundation models, human-centered AI, and human–robot interaction without mentioning or discussing Digital Twins. Since Digital Twins are not a relevant or central concept here, it does not meet IC1. Therefore, it is clearly unrelated to Digital Twins and should be excluded in Phase 1.

title: Anchoring autonomy: understanding seafarers’ interaction with energy efficiency decision support systems for route planning and the role of basic psychological needs
justification: IC1 not met: the abstract does not mention or position Digital Twins as a relevant or central concept; it focuses on seafarers’ interaction with a maritime route-planning decision support system. Although human-centered aspects are discussed, without any Digital Twin relevance the study clearly falls under EC1 (unrelated to Digital Twins).

title: Reinforcement learning versus data-driven dynamic programming: a comparison for finite horizon dynamic pricing markets
justification: The article focuses on comparing RL and DP methods for dynamic pricing in revenue management and does not mention or relate to Digital Twins (violates IC1). It also lacks any discussable explainability, transparency, or human-centered aspects (violates IC2). This is a clear case under EC1 (unrelated to Digital Twins).

title: Transforming phenomenological sociology for virtual personalities and virtual worlds
justification: The article is a philosophical/sociological discussion of AI-generated virtual personalities and virtual worlds. It does not mention or frame Digital Twins as a relevant concept of any system, architecture, or framework (violates IC1). While human interaction and issues like hallucination are discussed, they are not in the context of Digital Twins. Therefore, it clearly falls under EC1 (unrelated to Digital Twins).

title: NDLSC: A New Deep Learning-based Approach to Smart Contract Vulnerability Detection
justification: The article focuses on deep learning for smart contract vulnerability detection in blockchain and does not mention Digital Twins. It also does not address explainability or human-centered aspects in a Digital Twin context. Therefore, it clearly violates EC1 (unrelated to Digital Twins).

title: On the use of large language models in model-driven engineering
justification: The abstract focuses on large language models in model-driven engineering and does not mention Digital Twins or explainability/human interaction in the context of Digital Twins. It clearly violates EC1 (unrelated to Digital Twins).

title: Convergence of evolving artificial intelligence and machine learning techniques in precision oncology
justification: The abstract mentions digital twins (as synthetic data to aid clinical trials), indicating relevance to Digital Twins. It also references human-centered/interaction aspects like incorporation into clinical workflow and data sharing/generalizability. However, Digital Twins do not appear to be the central focus, and the linkage to explainability or human aspects specifically in the context of Digital Twins is unclear from the abstract. Not clearly a secondary study. Given Phase 1’s high recall, this is potentially relevant.

title: Machine learning for smart water distribution systems: exploring applications, challenges and future perspectives
justification: The article is an application-oriented survey on machine learning for smart water distribution systems and does not mention or center on Digital Twins (violates EC1). It is also a secondary study (survey), which is excluded under EC3. Although explainability is mentioned, it is not in the context of Digital Twins, so IC1 is not met.

title: Quantitative Semantic Models in Digital Twin Representations of Rock Masses Using Universal Discontinuity Index (UDi)
justification: Digital Twin models are central (integration of UDi into DT representations). While the abstract does not explicitly mention explainability/XAI or human interaction, it emphasizes semantic categories and a stress–strain ontology in the DT, which plausibly relates to interpretability/transparent representation. Not a review or non-peer-reviewed item, and in English. Given potential relevance to interpretability, mark as maybe for Phase 1.

title: Real-to-sim: automatic simulation model generation for a digital twin in semiconductor manufacturing
justification: Digital Twin is relevant, but the article focuses exclusively on automated simulation model generation and machine learning-based equipment emulation. The abstract does not mention explainability, interpretability, transparency, XAI, or human-centered/interaction aspects. This clearly meets EC2.

title: Researchers’ perceptions of automating scientific research
justification: Fails IC1: the abstract does not mention or discuss Digital Twins as a relevant concept. While explainability and human-centered aspects are addressed, EC1 applies because the article is clearly about AI/ML automation in scientific practice without any Digital Twin context.

title: Multi-stage tool wear prediction method based on multi-dimensional digital twin
justification: Digital Twin is central, but the article focuses on tool wear prediction and stage identification using a multidimensional DT, particle filtering, and SPC, with no mention of explainability, interpretability, transparency, XAI, or human interaction. This clearly fits EC2 (predictive/simulation focus without human/XAI aspects).

title: A Digital Twin System for Rock Triaxial Mechanical Tests Incorporating Probabilistic Parameter Updates and Model Prediction Through Data Assimilation Technique
justification: Digital Twin is central (IC1), but the study focuses exclusively on numerical model updating, data assimilation, and prediction for rock mechanics without any mention of explainability, interpretability, transparency, or human-centered/interaction aspects. This clearly meets EC2.

title: Privacy-preserving approach for IoT networks using statistical learning with optimization algorithm on high-dimensional big data environment
justification: The article focuses on privacy-preserving machine learning for IoT networks and intrusion detection, with no mention of Digital Twins. It therefore fails IC1 and clearly meets EC1 (unrelated to Digital Twins). Additionally, no explainability or human-interaction aspects are indicated.

title: Predicting the urban water demand by equipping intelligent-based methods with discrete wavelet transform function
justification: Fails IC1: the article does not discuss Digital Twins; it focuses on AI-based water demand prediction with wavelet transforms. No mention of explainability, transparency, or human interaction. Thus it clearly violates EC1.

title: Environment scan of generative AI infrastructure for clinical and translational science
justification: The article focuses on generative AI infrastructure, governance, and concerns (e.g., data security, clinician trust, AI bias) within clinical and translational science and does not mention or address Digital Twins. It clearly fails IC1 and meets EC1 as unrelated to Digital Twins.

title: Tool wear prediction based on XGBoost feature selection combined with PSO-BP network
justification: The article focuses on tool wear prediction using XGBoost and PSO-BP for CNC machining and does not mention or relate to Digital Twins, nor to explainability or human interaction aspects. This clearly violates IC1 and meets EC1 (unrelated to Digital Twins).

title: A new ontology-based approach to automatic information extraction from speech for production disturbance management
justification: The article focuses on ontology-based NLP to extract knowledge from production meeting speech for disturbance management and does not mention or relate to Digital Twins. Despite human-centered aspects (speech, interpretable texts), there is no Digital Twin context, failing IC1. Therefore, it clearly falls under EC1 (unrelated to Digital Twins).

title: Discovering ship maneuvering models from data
justification: The article focuses on data-driven system identification for ship maneuvering models and does not mention Digital Twins or any explainability/human interaction aspects. It fails IC1 and clearly meets EC1.

title: Open BIM exchange on Blockchain 3.0 virtual disk: A traceable semantic differential transaction approach
justification: The article focuses on BIM data exchange and blockchain-based traceability, with no mention of Digital Twins. It does not discuss explainability or human interaction in the context of Digital Twins, thus failing IC1. This is a clear case of EC1 (unrelated to Digital Twins).

title: A generative pre-trained transformer industrial bot to improve operators’ working experience in a small Industry 5.0 factory
justification: The article focuses on a GPT-based industrial bot for Industry 5.0, emphasizing operator support and human well-being. There is no mention or clear discussion of Digital Twins as a concept, system, or framework. While human-centered aspects are present, IC1 (Digital Twin relevance) is not satisfied. Therefore, it clearly violates EC1 (unrelated to Digital Twins).

title: A behavioral perspective on visualization in manufacturing and operations management: a review, framework, and research agenda
justification: The article is a secondary study (systematic review) on visualizations in manufacturing/operations and does not mention Digital Twins. It violates EC3 (secondary study) and clearly fails IC1 (Digital Twin not a relevant/central concept).

title: MetaCoorNet: an improved generated residual network for grasping pose estimation
justification: The article focuses on a deep learning architecture for robotic grasping pose estimation and does not mention or relate to Digital Twins. It also lacks any discussIon of explainability, transparency, or human-interaction aspects. Therefore, it clearly fails IC1 and meets EC1 (unrelated to Digital Twins).

title: Predictive Analytics Solution for Digital Capabilities Identification Towards Business Performance Improvement
justification: EC1: The article is clearly unrelated to Digital Twins; it focuses on digital transformation and predictive analytics for classifying literature. EC3: It is a secondary study analyzing 423 articles. It does not address explainability or human interaction in the context of Digital Twins, so IC1 and IC2 are not met.

title: Towards a decision support system for post bariatric hypoglycaemia: development of forecasting algorithms in unrestricted daily-life conditions
justification: The article focuses on forecasting algorithms and a decision support system for post-bariatric hypoglycaemia, with no mention of Digital Twins. It clearly fails IC1 and thus meets EC1 (unrelated to Digital Twins).

title: Mapping the emergence and maturation of sustainable supply chain technologies: a patent-based assessment of technology life cycles
justification: The article is a patent-based analysis of sustainable supply chain technologies and does not mention or discuss Digital Twins. It focuses on technology life cycles and topic modeling of patents, with no Digital Twin context or human/explainability aspects. Fails IC1 and clearly meets EC1.

title: Large language models for building energy applications: Opportunities and challenges
justification: The article focuses on large language models for building energy applications and does not mention or discuss Digital Twins. It therefore fails IC1. Given the absence of any Digital Twin context, it clearly meets EC1 (unrelated to Digital Twins).

title: Vision-based sensing and digital twin technologies in conformal 3D concrete printing: exploring operational accuracy, adaptability, and scalability, and investigating monitoring capabilities in large-scale applications
justification: Digital Twin is a central concept (DTs for 3D concrete printing) and the abstract explicitly discusses real-time monitoring and identifying/quantifying discrepancies between planned and executed deposition, which relates to transparency aspects. This satisfies IC1 and IC2 for Phase 1.

title: Datafication Research (1994–2023): Three Decades of Evolving Methodology in Data Science
justification: The article is a bibliometric/overview study of datafication and does not mention Digital Twins or discuss explainability/human interaction in a Digital Twin context. It clearly violates EC1 (unrelated to Digital Twins) and EC3 (secondary study).

title: Explainable digital twins for circular construction: A systematic review of real-time decision-making and urban retrofitting frameworks
justification: The article is a systematic review (secondary study) explicitly stated in the title and abstract (PRISMA-guided review), which falls under EC3 exclusion criteria, despite its clear relevance to Digital Twins and explainability.

title: Shaping the future of nuclear reactors with digital twins: Current developments and perspectives
justification: The article is explicitly a review/secondary study (“This review synthesizes the state of the field”), which meets EC3 for exclusion, despite Digital Twins being central and interpretability/trust issues being discussed.

title: A systematic review of transformers and large language models in the energy sector: towards agentic digital twins
justification: Although Digital Twins are central and human/interaction aspects (e.g., social interaction, autonomy) are discussed, the article is explicitly a systematic review (secondary study). Per EC3, secondary studies are excluded in Phase 1.

title: DIGITAL TWIN–BASED INTELLIGENT MONITORING OF INDUSTRIAL SYSTEMS USING EXPLAINABLE AI
justification: Meets IC1 and IC2: Digital Twin is central (HADT-C-XAI hybrid digital twin framework) and the work explicitly addresses explainability and human interaction (feature attribution, interpretable fault causes, operator decision support). English research article; not a secondary study.

title: Digital Twin Framework for Predictive Simulation and Decision Support in Ship Damage Control
justification: Digital Twin is the central focus (DT framework for ship damage control). The abstract explicitly addresses human-centered and interaction aspects (human-in-the-loop, human approval/override, human–machine collaboration, human-centric operation) alongside decision support. This satisfies IC1 and IC2; it is not exclusively predictive/simulation-only. Peer-reviewed with English abstract.

title: A Bidirectional Digital Twin System for Adaptive Manufacturing
justification: Digital Twin is the central focus (bidirectional DTS architecture for CNC milling), and the abstract explicitly references interpretability (“foundation for scalable, interpretable digital twins”), satisfying IC1 and IC2. It is a peer-reviewed research article with an English abstract and is not limited to simulation-only aspects. Therefore it clearly meets Phase 1 inclusion criteria.

title: Digital Twins Under EU Law: A Unified Compliance Framework Across Smart Cities, Industry, Transportation, and Energy Systems
justification: Digital Twins are the central focus and the article discusses transparency/explainability and human-centric aspects, satisfying IC1 and IC2. However, it is explicitly a scoping review using PRISMA-ScR and thus a secondary study, which meets EC3 for exclusion in Phase 1.

title: A digital twin model for grain enterprise financial shared service centers based on distributed deep learning and neural symbolic reasoning
justification: Digital Twin is central (a comprehensive DT model for financial shared service centers) and the abstract explicitly highlights interpretability and interpretable decision support via neural symbolic reasoning, knowledge graphs, and rule-based inference. This satisfies IC1 and IC2. It is a peer-reviewed article with an English abstract, so no exclusion criteria apply.

title: Digital twin based deep learning framework for personalized thermal comfort prediction and energy efficient operation in smart buildings
justification: Digital Twin is central to the proposed framework (IC1), and the study explicitly addresses explainability and interpretability via attention mechanisms and XAI methods (SHAP, LIME) in an occupant-centric context (IC2). It is peer-reviewed and in English, with no clear exclusion criteria met.

title: Rule-based symbolic AI computing-driven digital twin model for ex-ante energy evaluation of task-ambience air conditioning systems in zero-energy buildings
justification: Digital twin is the core of the proposed model (IC1). The abstract explicitly mentions an interactive VR-based assessment framework for designers and describes the framework as real-time and explainable, addressing human interaction and explainability aspects (IC2). No exclusion criteria apply.

title: AI-Assisted Design of Custom Insoles for Plantar Pressure Redistribution via a Digital Twin Framework
justification: Digital Twin is central (AI-assisted digital twin framework for custom insoles), and explainability is explicitly addressed via SHAP to enhance interpretability and trust. Also mentions human-centered personalization and clinical relevance. Meets IC1 and IC2; none of the exclusion criteria apply.

title: Artificial Intelligence and Digital Twins for Sustainable Production Systems
justification: The article is a bibliometric/content analysis of 118 publications (a secondary study), which falls under EC3. Although Digital Twins and explainable/human-centric aspects are discussed (meeting IC1 and IC2), it is clearly a survey/review rather than a primary study or conceptual/system proposal, thus excluded in Phase 1.

title: From Forecasting to Foresight: Building an Autonomous O&M Brain for the New Power System Based on a Cognitive Digital Twin
justification: Central focus on a Cognitive Digital Twin for power system O&M (IC1) and explicit mention of transparent and explainable decision-making (IC2). Meets Phase 1 inclusion; none of the exclusions apply.

title: Mixed Reality-Based Multi-Scenario Visualization and Control in Automated Terminals: A Middleware and Digital Twin Driven Approach
justification: Digital Twin is central (DT–MR framework for automated terminals) and the article emphasizes human-centered interaction (Mixed Reality interface with gaze/gesture/voice, safety interlocks, human-in-the-loop supervision). This satisfies IC1 and IC2(b). It is a peer-reviewed journal article and not a secondary study.

title: Interception well digital twin for early warning of combined sewer overflows
justification: Digital Twin is central (framework for interception wells), and the abstract explicitly mentions enhancing interpretability of field data, satisfying IC1 and IC2. No exclusion criteria clearly apply.

title: Agent-to-Agent (A2A) Protocol Integrated Digital Twin System with AgentIQ for Multimodal AI Fitness Coaching and Personalized Well-Being
justification: Digital Twin is central (protocol-integrated DT architecture for fitness coaching), and the work explicitly addresses explainability/transparency (e.g., 'explainable', observability with AgentIQ/LangSmith) and human-centered interaction (real-time multimodal feedback, embodied avatars, emotionally adaptive coaching). Peer-reviewed conference paper in English; not a secondary study.

title: A five-dimensional digital twin framework driven by large language models-enhanced RL for CNC systems
justification: Digital Twins are central (a five-dimensional DT framework for CNC systems). While the abstract does not explicitly discuss explainability or transparency, it references human expertise reliance in CNC systems and mentions personalized services, suggesting potential human-related aspects. Given Phase 1’s high-recall goal and the possibility of human-centered interaction elements in the proposed framework, this article may be relevant.

title: Towards Evolving Actor–Network Ontologies: Enabling Reflexive Digital Twins for Cultural Heritage
justification: Digital Twins are central (cultural digital twins) and the work explicitly addresses explainability/interpretability and human-centered aspects: it proposes a reflexive, actor–network-based ontology for DTs where semantic interpretations are negotiated among heterogeneous actors and emphasizes a transparent and interpretable framework. It appears to be a peer-reviewed article with an English abstract.

title: Engineering-Oriented Explainable Machine Learning and Digital Twin Framework for Sustainable Dairy Production and Environmental Impact Optimisation
justification: The article proposes an explainable machine learning and digital twin framework and integrates predictive models into a digital twin platform for decision support. It explicitly employs SHAP-based explainability. This clearly satisfies IC1 (Digital Twin central) and IC2 (explainability/human decision support), and none of the exclusion criteria apply.

title: PINN-DT: Optimizing Energy Consumption in Smart Building Using Hybrid Physics-Informed Neural Networks and Digital Twin Framework with Blockchain Security
justification: Digital Twins are a central component of the proposed framework (DRL agents trained with DT data; integration of DT, PINNs, and blockchain). The study mentions interpretability (via PINNs), transparency (via blockchain communication), and a user comfort index, satisfying the requirement for explainability/human-centered aspects in the DT context (IC1, IC2). Not a clear case for any exclusion.

title: Artificial intelligence and machine learning for smart grids: from foundational paradigms to emerging technologies with digital twin and large language model-driven intelligence
justification: The abstract explicitly states it is a comprehensive review (secondary study) of AI/ML in smart grids, including DT-driven intelligence. Per EC3, secondary studies (systematic reviews/surveys) are excluded in Phase 1, even though Digital Twins are discussed.

title: Toward digital twins in the intensive care unit: a medication management case study
justification: Digital Twins are a central focus (IC1), and the study relates to human-centered aspects via clinical decision support and treatment recommendations for ICU clinicians (IC2b). It is a peer-reviewed English article and not exclusively about predictive/simulation without human context, so it meets Phase 1 inclusion criteria.

title: Cerebrum twin: A 6D semantic digital twin of multi-lobe digital brain functions for human-centric Industry 5.0
justification: Central focus on a semantic Digital Twin (Cerebrum Twin) and explicitly addresses human-centered interaction (voice-based human interaction, operator-oriented decision-making, human-in-the-loop optimization) and transparency (“robust, transparent” decision-making). Meets IC1 and IC2. Peer-reviewed journal article with English abstract.

title: Knowledge Graphs and Artificial Intelligence for the Implementation of Cognitive Heritage Digital Twins
justification: Digital Twins are central (heritage digital twins), and the study explicitly addresses interpretability, transparency, bias mitigation, and human oversight. This satisfies IC1 and IC2. It is a peer-reviewed journal article in English and not limited to purely predictive/simulation models.

title: Ontology-Driven Digital Twin Framework for Aviation Maintenance and Operations
justification: Clearly meets IC1 and IC2: Digital Twin is the central focus (ontology-driven DT framework for aviation) and the abstract explicitly addresses explainable decision support, transparent and traceable reasoning, and explainable inference. Peer-reviewed journal with English title/abstract. Not a secondary study or purely predictive model.

title: Life prediction and health assessment of aero-engine gas path using digital twin and deep learning
justification: Digital Twin is a central component of the proposed health monitoring system (IC1). The abstract explicitly mentions a three-dimensional visualization interaction framework to improve observability and interpretability, and a multi-level virtual-reality interaction mechanism linking physical space, assessment, and decision-making (IC2: explainability/interpretability and human interaction). Peer-reviewed, English abstract. Clearly satisfies Phase 1 inclusion.

title: Innovative integration of computer vision, IoT, and digital twin in food quality and safety assessment
justification: Although the article discusses Digital Twins and touches on transparency and interpretability, it is explicitly a review (secondary study). Per EC3, secondary studies (systematic reviews/surveys) are excluded in Phase 1.

title: Artificial intelligence and digital twins for the personalised prediction of hypertension risk
justification: The article is explicitly a review (secondary study) examining AI/ML and the potential of digital twins, and while it mentions explainability and transparency, EC3 excludes secondary studies such as reviews or surveys. Therefore, it clearly violates Phase 1 exclusion criteria.

title: Advances in artificial intelligence and digital twin for tunnel boring machines
justification: The article explicitly describes itself as a systematic review of AI in tunnel boring machines and is published in a review journal. Although it proposes a DT-based architecture and discusses model interpretability (meeting IC1 and IC2), it is clearly a secondary study, which meets EC3 for Phase 1 exclusion.

title: Digital twins and AI for healthy and sustainable cities
justification: Digital Twins are a central concept in the article (urban digital twins discussed and their articulation). The abstract addresses human-centered aspects (management of expectations, alignment within a social setting, policy decision-makers), satisfying IC1 and IC2(b). It is a peer-reviewed journal article and not clearly a secondary study. High-recall phase warrants inclusion.

title: Beyond digital twins: the role of foundation models in enhancing the interpretability of multiomics modalities in precision medicine
justification: The article is explicitly a review (secondary study) discussing integration of foundation models into medical digital twins to enhance interpretability. Despite relevance to digital twins and explainability, EC3 excludes secondary studies in Phase 1.

title: A survey of cognitive digital twin and the potential use of LLMs
justification: The article is a secondary study (survey/systematic review) on cognitive digital twins and LLMs. Per EC3, surveys are excluded. While Digital Twins are central and human/XAI-related aspects may be discussed, the study type clearly violates EC3.

title: Digital Convergence in Dental Informatics: A Structured Narrative Review of Artificial Intelligence, Internet of Things, Digital Twins, and Large Language Models with Security, Privacy, and Ethical Perspectives
justification: EC3: This is a structured narrative review (secondary study). Although it discusses Digital Twins and ethics/transparency, it is not a primary research article, so it clearly violates Phase 1 exclusion criteria.

title: A Framework for Standardizing the Development of Serious Games with Real-Time Self-Adaptation Capabilities Using Digital Twins
justification: Digital Twins are central to the proposed framework for self-adaptive serious games (IC1). The abstract explicitly references interpretability/comprehension via semantic annotation and ontologies, and emphasizes human-centered interaction and personalization (real-time adaptation to players, expert-defined rules, usability evaluation) (IC2). No exclusion criteria clearly apply.

title: An Integrated Approach to Real-Time 3D Sensor Data Visualization for Digital Twin Applications
justification: Digital Twin is central to the study (visualization for DT applications), and the abstract explicitly addresses human-centered interpretability (e.g., ‘intuitive understanding,’ ‘at-a-glance comprehension,’ and ‘enhanced data interpretability through ramp shading’). This satisfies IC1 and IC2, so it should be included in Phase 1.

title: SmartGridAgent: An Educational Framework for Reliable Digital Twin-Based Smart Grid Workforce Training with Locally Hosted LLMs
justification: Digital Twin is central (digital twin-based smart grid framework) and the article addresses human-centered aspects (workforce training, educational platform, curriculum guidelines) alongside trustworthiness concerns of AI/LLMs in DT-based systems. This satisfies IC1 and the human interaction aspect of IC2; it is not exclusively about predictive/simulation models.

title: A systematic review of AI as a digital twin for prostate cancer care
justification: EC3 applies: the article is explicitly a systematic review (secondary study). While it clearly involves Digital Twins (IC1) and mentions explainability (IC2), Phase 1 excludes surveys/systematic reviews.

title: Healthcare system optimization using digital twin
justification: Digital Twin is a central concept for healthcare optimization, and the study explicitly addresses interpretability and human interaction via a GUI that provides clear visual representation of patient criticality. This satisfies IC1 and IC2. No clear exclusion criteria apply.

title: Advanced User Interaction with Urban Digital Twins using Large Language Models
justification: Digital Twin is central (Urban Digital Twin framework) and the study focuses on human-centered interaction via LLMs enabling natural language queries and visualization for stakeholders. This satisfies IC1 and IC2 through human interaction aspects; no clear exclusion criteria apply.

title: Implementing an AI-Based Digital Twin Analysis System for Real-Time Decision Support in a Custom-Made Sportswear SME
justification: Digital twin is central (AI-enhanced digital twin implementation in an SME), and the abstract explicitly addresses explainability/human-centered aspects (interpretable visual insights, human-centered decision-making, and improved process transparency). Meets IC1 and IC2; none of the exclusion criteria apply.

title: Agentic AI for Cultural Heritage: Embedding Risk Memory in Semantic Digital Twins
justification: Digital Twins are central (semantic digital twins in cultural heritage), and the work explicitly addresses transparency and structured, explainable reasoning supporting human decision-making. Meets IC1 and IC2; no clear exclusion criteria apply.

title: Theories and Technologies of Intelligent Digital Twin Modeling for Optical Networks (Invited)
justification: Digital Twins are the central focus (intelligent DT modeling for optical networks), and the abstract explicitly addresses interpretability (white-box models providing strong interpretability, contrast with black-box and grey-box) and trustworthiness. This satisfies IC1 and IC2. No clear exclusion applies (it is a peer-reviewed journal article; not exclusively predictive without interpretability/human aspects).

title: Enhancing medical digital twins within metaverse using blockchain, NFTs and LLMs
justification: Digital Twins (medical digital twins) are the central focus (IC1). The work explicitly addresses human-centered interaction via an LLM-powered NPC in a metaverse and discusses user interaction, access control, and system architecture (IC2b). It is a peer-reviewed journal article in English and not limited to purely predictive/simulation models, so no exclusion criteria apply.

title: Integrating Machine Learning and Characterization in Battery Research: Toward Cognitive Digital Twins with Physics and Knowledge
justification: The abstract explicitly states it is a review article (“This review explores...”), which is a secondary study. EC3 excludes secondary studies. Although it discusses cognitive digital twins and interpretability/transparency (meeting IC1 and IC2), the clear review nature triggers exclusion in Phase 1.

title: Physics-informed digital twin design for supporting the selection of process settings in continuous manufacturing, with a focus in fiberboard production
justification: Digital Twin is central (physics-informed DT framework for process settings in continuous manufacturing). The article explicitly addresses interpretability (“interpretable model architecture”) and human-centric/interaction aspects (operator decision-making, balancing technical and human aspects like operator workload). Meets IC1 and IC2; none of the exclusion criteria apply.

title: Metaverse and Digital Twins in the Age of AI and Extended Reality
justification: Digital Twins are a central focus, examined alongside the Metaverse in architectural contexts (IC1). The article explicitly addresses human-centered and interaction aspects—multi-user engagement, immersive user experiences, AI-driven collaboration, and LLM-powered agents within DT/virtual environments—meeting the requirement for human interaction aspects (IC2). It is peer-reviewed and in English, with no clear exclusion criteria triggered.

title: Models vs infrastructures? On the role of digital twins’ hype in anticipating the governance of the UK energy industry
justification: Digital twins are the central focus (energy sector governance) and the abstract explicitly references explainability, transparency, and public engagement (human-centered aspects). This satisfies IC1 and IC2 for Phase 1.

title: Innovative AI strategies for enhancing smart building operations through digital twins: A survey
justification: The article is a survey (secondary study), which is excluded by EC3. Additionally, the abstract focuses on AI techniques for DT in smart buildings (predictive scenarios, anomaly detection, optimization) without mentioning explainability, transparency, or human-centered interaction aspects, aligning with EC2.

title: Deep Learning Approaches to Natural Language Processing for Digital Twins of Patients in Psychiatry and Neurological Rehabilitation
justification: Digital Twins are central to the article (patient DTs in psychiatry/neurological rehab), and it explicitly mentions explainability and human-centered aspects (patient trust, safety, ethics) in the DT context. Meets IC1 and IC2; none of the exclusion criteria apply.

title: Redefining Research Crowdsourcing Incorporating Human Feedback with LLM-Powered Digital Twins
justification: Digital Twins are a central concept (LLM-powered, personalized AI models emulating worker behavior) and the study explicitly addresses human-centered aspects (human-in-the-loop, worker agency) and transparency. It meets IC1 and IC2; none of the exclusion criteria apply.

title: Constructing Enterprise Digital Twins by Augmenting LLMs with MDE
justification: Digital Twins are central (constructing Enterprise Digital Twins). The abstract discusses human-centered/interaction aspects (coordination between domain experts and modelers, alleviating cognitive burden, stakeholders), satisfying IC1 and IC2(b). It is a peer-reviewed conference paper in English and does not fall under exclusions.

title: Agentic AI for Digital Twin
justification: Digital Twins are central (agentic LLMs interfacing with digital twins in shipping), and the work explicitly addresses human-centered interaction by using language as a universal interface for stakeholders and supporting user-specific queries and interactive decision-making. It is a peer-reviewed proceedings paper, not a secondary study. Meets IC1 and IC2(b).

title: HyBaTwin: Web-Based Hybrid Digital Twin Platform for Electric Vehicle Battery Capacity Estimation
justification: Digital Twin is the core focus (web-based hybrid DT for EV battery BMS), and the study explicitly employs XAI to select trustworthy and explainable approaches. This satisfies IC1 and IC2. It is a peer-reviewed journal article with an English abstract. Not excluded by any EC.

title: Leveraging Immersive Digital Twins and AI-Driven Decision Support Systems for Sustainable Water Reserves Management: A Conceptual Framework
justification: Digital Twins are a central element of the proposed conceptual framework (IC1). The abstract explicitly addresses human-centered and interaction aspects—immersive decision-making, RAG chatbots, stakeholder communication, participatory decision-making—and mentions transparency in decision processes (IC2). It is in English and appears peer-reviewed. Therefore, it clearly satisfies Phase 1 inclusion criteria.

title: Uncertainty quantification in real-time parameter updating for digital twins using Bayesian inverse mapping models

Peer-reviewed and in English. Meets IC1 and IC2.

title: Cognitive Digital Twins for Improving Security in IT-OT Enabled Healthcare Applications
justification: Digital Twins are central (Cognitive Digital Twins framework for healthcare IT-OT security), and the work explicitly includes human-centered aspects via a human-in-the-loop decision-making approach and a cognitive cycle. Meets IC1 and IC2(b); no clear exclusion applies.

title: Synergizing First-Principles and Machine Learning: Predicting Steel Flatness in the Era of Digital Twins and Physics-Informed Intelligence
justification: Digital Twin is central (a state-of-the-art digital twin structure with software agents), and the work explicitly emphasizes transparency and interpretability alongside predictive modeling. Thus it meets IC1 and IC2. It appears to be a primary research contribution, not a secondary study.

title: Harnessing Machine Learning, Blockchain, and Digital Twin Technology for Advanced Robotics in Manufacturing: Challenges and Future Directions
justification: Digital Twin is highlighted in the title, indicating relevance, and the abstract mentions model interpretability (an explainability aspect). While the abstract does not explicitly link explainability to Digital Twins and the piece may be a broad review chapter, there is potential relevance. Given Phase 1’s high-recall aim and unclear linkage, retain as maybe for further screening.

title: Digital Twin and Foundation Models: A New Frontier
justification: Digital Twins are the central focus (integration of foundation models into DTs), and the abstract explicitly mentions transparency and interpretability in AI decision-making within DTs. This satisfies IC1 and IC2. It appears to be a peer-reviewed conference position paper, not a secondary study.

title: Reality anchor methodology: how to design a digital twin to support situation awareness
justification: Digital Twin is the central focus (designing a DT as a decision support system), and the work emphasizes human-centered aspects—situation awareness, integrating users’ abilities, human-in-the-loop testing, and user task analysis—meeting IC1 and IC2.

title: Enabling trustworthiness in human-swarm systems through a digital twin
justification: Digital Twin is central (a platform for human-swarm teaming) and the work explicitly addresses explainability, trustworthiness, and human supervision/interaction. Clearly satisfies IC1 and IC2. Not a secondary study or non-peer-reviewed short piece.

title: Blockchain-enabled digital twin system for brain stroke prediction
justification: Digital Twin is central (healthcare DT for stroke prediction). While the abstract emphasizes security/privacy via blockchain (tamper-proof, anomaly detection), it does not explicitly mention explainability, interpretability, or human interaction. However, blockchain-related transparency/trust aspects may be relevant to IC2. Given Phase 1’s high-recall rule, mark as potential relevance.

title: The Impact of Predictive Maintenance on the Performance of Industrial Enterprises
justification: The article focuses on predictive maintenance using IoT/AI/ML and business performance, with no mention of Digital Twins or explainability/human-centered aspects. It clearly violates IC1 and falls under EC1 (unrelated to Digital Twins).

title: Implementation of an AI-based predictive structural health monitoring strategy for bonded insulated rail joints using digital twins under varied bolt conditions
justification: While Digital Twin is central (IC1), the abstract focuses solely on predictive classification and performance evaluation for structural health monitoring with no mention of explainability, interpretability, transparency, XAI, or human-centered/interaction aspects. This clearly meets EC2, so it is excluded in Phase 1.

title: A Symbolic AI Approach to Medical Training
justification: The article focuses on a symbolic AI and simulation-based medical training system (GLARE-Edu) grounded in clinical guidelines. There is no mention or indication of Digital Twins as a relevant or central concept. While human interaction and training aspects are present, the Digital Twin criterion (IC1) is not met. Therefore, it clearly falls under EC1 (unrelated to Digital Twins).

title: Digital Twin for Health Monitoring of a Cantilever Beam Using Support Vector Machine
justification: Digital Twin is central, but the study focuses on SVM-based predictive classification for structural health monitoring without any mention of explainability, interpretability, transparency, or human interaction aspects. This clearly meets EC2 (exclusive focus on predictive/simulation models within DTs without human/XAI elements).

title: Predecting power transformer health index and life expectation based on digital twins and multitask LSTM-GRU model
justification: Digital Twins are central via the SEMS-FDT architecture, and the study explicitly incorporates explainability (global and local model explanations) to aid engineers. This meets IC1 and IC2; it is a peer-reviewed English article.

title: Feasibility of a clouds and edge computing scheme for internal due date assignment in advanced manufacturing systems
justification: The article does not discuss Digital Twins; it focuses on a cloud/edge computing scheme using DNN and RF for due date assignment in manufacturing. Without Digital Twin as a relevant concept, it fails IC1 and clearly meets EC1 (unrelated to Digital Twins).

title: Deep learning based approaches for intelligent industrial machinery health management and fault diagnosis in resource-constrained environments
justification: Clear secondary study (survey) focusing on intelligent fault diagnosis, RUL prediction, and edge architectures without mention of Digital Twins or explainability/human interaction aspects. Violates EC3 (secondary study), and based on the abstract appears unrelated to Digital Twins (EC1) and centered on predictive models without XAI or human aspects (EC2).

title: Optimized VMD and novel ECK-Venn based approach to IMF selection for chatter and tool wear classification
justification: The abstract does not mention or relate to Digital Twins (violates EC1). It focuses on signal processing and deep learning (VMD, IMF selection, spectrograms, CNN-MobileNet) for chatter and tool wear classification without any explainability or human-centered aspects, which would also fall under EC2 if in a DT context. Therefore, it clearly fails the Phase 1 inclusion criteria.

title: Research on the high precision hydraulic column stress monitoring method
justification: Fails IC1: The article does not discuss Digital Twins. It focuses on a high-precision stress monitoring method for hydraulic columns using combined data-driven and mechanism models, with no mention of digital twins, explainability, or human interaction aspects. Clearly unrelated to Digital Twins (EC1) and focuses on monitoring/predictive modeling without human-centered or explainability components (EC2).

title: A novel method for intelligent operation and maintenance of transformers using deep visual large model DETR + X and digital twin
justification: Digital twin is central to the proposed framework for transformer monitoring and maintenance. The inclusion of an expert decision-making tool (LLaVA-7b) that provides operational recommendations suggests human-centered decision support, though the abstract does not explicitly discuss explainability or transparency. Given the high-recall phase and potential human-interaction relevance, this article is a potential fit.

title: Quantum machine learning for Lyapunov-stabilized computation offloading in next-generation MEC networks
justification: The article focuses on quantum machine learning for computation offloading in MEC networks with Lyapunov optimization. It does not mention Digital Twins, nor does it address explainability, transparency, or human interaction aspects. This clearly violates EC1 (unrelated to Digital Twins).

title: Towards Build Optimization Using Digital Twins - Proceedings of the 21st International Conference on Predictive Models and Data Analytics in Software Engineering
justification: IC1 is clearly met: the paper centers on a Digital Twin framework (CBDT) for CI build processes. While the abstract does not explicitly mention explainability or human-centered interaction, the described digital shadowing, real-time monitoring of performance metrics, and prescriptive services suggest potential human-in-the-loop use (e.g., developers/DevOps interacting with monitoring/decision support). Given Phase 1’s high-recall goal and absence of a clear EC2 violation, this has potential relevance and should not be excluded at this stage.

title: Agentic AI for digital twin - Proceedings of the Thirty-Ninth AAAI Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Thirty-Seventh Conference on Innovative Applications of Artificial Intelligence and Fifteenth Symposium on Educational Advances in Artificial Intelligence
justification: Digital twin is the central focus (IC1), and the work introduces a language-based, interactive interface for human stakeholders (technicians, fleet managers), clearly addressing human-centered interaction aspects (IC2). No clear exclusion criteria apply.

title: Data Storytelling to Unlock the Communicative Power of Digital Twins - Database and Expert Systems Applications: 36th International Conference, DEXA 2025, Bangkok, Thailand, August 25–27, 2025, Proceedings, Part II
justification: Digital Twins are the central focus (user-centered workflow integrated into environmental DTs), and the paper explicitly addresses human-centered communication and interpretability (accessible, interpretable, actionable insights, data storytelling for diverse audiences). This satisfies IC1 and IC2 for Phase 1.

title: Toward Reliable Pavement Digital Twins: Multi-Scale Spatiotemporal Monitoring Challenges and Solutions - Proceedings of the 1st ACM SIGSPATIAL International Workshop on Spatial Intelligence for Smart and Connected Communities
justification: Digital Twin is central (pavement digital twins and a two-tier framework). The work addresses transparency/interpretability aspects via Bayesian uncertainty quantification with confidence intervals, verifiable measures, and QA/QC, and supports human decision-making (“right time, right location, right treatment”). Meets IC1 and IC2; not a clear case for exclusion.

title: Digital Twins in Security Operations: State of the Art and Future Perspectives
justification: The article is a secondary study (survey/structured literature review) in ACM Computing Surveys, which falls under EC3 and is excluded in Phase 1 despite Digital Twins being central.

title: Large Language Models for Explainable Decisions in Dynamic Digital Twins - Dynamic Data Driven Applications Systems: 5th International Conference, DDDAS/Infosymbiotics for Reliable AI 2024, New Brunswick, NJ, USA, November 6–8, 2024, Proceedings
justification: Clearly satisfies IC1 and IC2: Digital Twins (DDTs) are the central focus, and the paper explicitly explores explainability via LLM-generated natural language explanations for decision-making within DDTs. It appears to be a peer-reviewed conference proceeding with an English title/abstract, and is not a secondary study.

title: Nested Multi-objective Model Updating for an Aircraft Wingtail Digital Twin - Proceedings of the Genetic and Evolutionary Computation Conference Companion
justification: Digital Twin is central, but the article focuses exclusively on model updating/optimization of FEM and reduced-order models for efficiency and accuracy in a DT. The abstract contains no mention of explainability, interpretability, transparency, or human-centered/interaction aspects. This clearly meets EC2 for exclusion in Phase 1.

title: Robust and expert-agnostic digital twin calibration via ensemble learning and Bayesian optimization - Proceedings of the 12th ACM International Conference on Systems for Energy-Efficient Buildings, Cities, and Transportation
justification: Digital Twin is a central focus (calibration of DT models). The abstract references human-related aspects by aiming to remove reliance on domain experts ('expert-agnostic' parameter screening), but it does not clearly address explainability/interpretability/transparency. Given Phase 1’s high-recall goal, it has potential relevance to human-centered aspects in DTs, though evidence is not explicit.

title: Semantic-aware LLM orchestration for proactive resource management in predictive digital twin vehicular networks
justification: Digital Twin is central (predictive digital twin for vehicular networks), and the framework explicitly incorporates human interaction via natural-language semantic commands and converting human intent into network behavior. This satisfies IC1 and the human-centered aspect of IC2. Not a clear exclusion case.

title: Comparative Analysis of Motif-Based Anomaly Detection for Humidity Monitoring in Digital Twin Systems - Proceedings of the IEEE/ACM 12th International Conference on Big Data Computing, Applications and Technologies
justification: Digital Twins are a central application context (IC1). The study references expert-labeled validation and confidence scores, indicating some human-related aspects, though explainability/XAI is not explicit (partial IC2). It is not a clear exclusion under EC2. Given Phase 1 high recall, it is potentially relevant.

title: FlexiDigital: A Comprehensive Approach to Energy Flexibility Services using Digital Twins and Large Language Models - Proceedings of the 16th ACM International Conference on Future and Sustainable Energy Systems
justification: Digital Twins are central to the proposed framework (federated digital twins), and the work explicitly addresses human-centered interaction via AI-powered digital assistants, prosumer engagement, and user control of assets. This satisfies IC1 and the human interaction aspect of IC2. It is a conference proceedings position paper, not a secondary study. Therefore, it clearly meets Phase 1 inclusion criteria.

title: An X Language-Driven Framework for Systematic Development of Digital Twin Healthcare Systems
justification: Digital Twin Healthcare is the central focus (IC1), and the article explicitly addresses interpretability, trustworthiness, and transparency of DTH models, proposing a framework to develop interpretable and trustworthy DTs (IC2). It is a peer-reviewed journal article in English and does not fall under any exclusion criteria.

title: The Role of Multi-Agents in Digital Twin Implementation: Short Survey
justification: EC3: This is a secondary study ("Short Survey" in ACM Computing Surveys), which is excluded in Phase 1. Additionally, the abstract does not indicate explainability, transparency, or human-centered aspects in DTs, focusing instead on multi-agent roles and technology integration.

title: Optimizing Last-Mile Logistics with Digital Twins and Multi-agent Learning: Enhancing Efficiency, Customer Satisfaction, and Urban Integration
justification: Digital Twin is a central component of the proposed last‑mile logistics framework. The abstract references human-centered aspects, including stakeholder-driven decision-support, customer satisfaction, personalization options for consumers, and implications for city officials and logistics providers. This satisfies IC1 and the human interaction aspect of IC2. It is a peer-reviewed journal article in English and does not fall under clear exclusions.

title: Opportunities for Digital Twins for the Provisioning, Management and Monitoring of Heterogeneous IoT Devices - Proceedings of the ACM/IEEE 27th International Conference on Model Driven Engineering Languages and Systems
justification: Digital Twins are central to the proposed DaaS platform for lifecycle management of heterogeneous IoT devices (IC1). While the abstract focuses on provisioning, management, and monitoring, it does not explicitly mention explainability or human interaction with DTs. However, the management/monitoring context implies potential human-centered interaction with DT-based representations. Given Phase 1’s high-recall goal and potential relevance to human-in-the-loop operations, mark as 'maybe' for further screening.

title: Challenges and Opportunities in Secure Real-Time Digital Twin Systems for AR/VR-Enabled Smart Factories - Proceedings of the International Workshop on Middleware for IT/OT Integration
justification: Digital Twin is a central focus (integrated real-time DT control architecture for AR/VR-enabled smart factories). The paper explicitly addresses human-centered and interaction aspects (AR/VR operator support, human–machine collaboration, human-centric DT ecosystems). This satisfies IC1 and the human-centered part of IC2. It is a workshop proceedings paper with a DOI and not clearly a poster/tutorial or secondary study.

title: Explainable modeling in digital twin - Proceedings of the Winter Simulation Conference
justification: Digital Twin is central (framework and case study on a DT factory), and the work explicitly addresses explainability and human interaction (stakeholder collaboration, automatically generated explanations, explainability scores). This satisfies IC1 and IC2. It appears to be a peer-reviewed conference proceeding, not a secondary study, so no clear exclusion applies.

title: Key technology of digital twin modeling for production process of flexible production line based on data - Proceedings of the 9th International Conference on Electronic Information Technology and Computer Engineering
justification: Digital Twin is central (framework for flexible production line). The paper describes human-facing aspects such as visual management, real-time monitoring, and an application presentation layer, indicating human interaction with the Digital Twin. This satisfies IC1 and IC2(b). It is a peer-reviewed conference paper with an English abstract.

title: How Digital Twins Can Help to Accelerate the Transition to a Carbon-Neutral System - Computer Aided Systems Theory – EUROCAST 2024: 19th International Conference, Las Palmas de Gran Canaria, Spain, February 25 – March 1, 2024, Revised Selected Papers, Part III
justification: Digital Twins are central to the work, and the article explicitly addresses human-centered aspects (decision makers, trust) and explainability/transparency as contributors to trust. This satisfies IC1 and IC2 and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

title: Blockchain-Based Digital Twins: Research Trends, Issues, and Future Challenges
justification: Clearly a secondary study (survey) in ACM Computing Surveys, which falls under EC3. While Digital Twins are central, the abstract does not indicate a focus on explainability, transparency, XAI, or human interaction, and EC3 alone is sufficient for exclusion in Phase 1.

title: Human-Autonomy Teaming on Autonomous Vehicles with Large Language Model-Enabled Human Digital Twins - Proceedings of the Eighth ACM/IEEE Symposium on Edge Computing
justification: Digital Twins (specifically Human Digital Twins) are central to the paper, and it explicitly focuses on human-autonomy teaming and human-machine interaction via LLM-enabled HDTs. This satisfies IC1 and the human-centered/interaction aspect of IC2. It is not exclusively about predictive/simulation models, and the abstract is in English and appears peer-reviewed.

title: How to regulate a Digital Twin City? Insights from a Proactive Law approach: How “human in the loop” and “precautionary principles” can serve policymakers in their attempt to incorporate respect of rights and solidarity in the smart city. - Proceedings of the 24th Annual International Conference ...
justification: Digital Twin City is the central focus (IC1). The paper explicitly discusses human-centered aspects via 'human in the loop' and governance principles for DTCs (IC2). It appears to be a peer-reviewed conference proceeding with an English title/abstract, so no clear exclusion applies.

title: Mathematical and Computational Foundations to Enable Predictive Digital Twins at Scale
justification: Digital Twins are central and interpretability is explicitly addressed (interpretable ML/classifier), satisfying IC1 and IC2. However, the item is a thesis (non-peer-reviewed), clearly triggering EC3. Therefore, exclude in Phase 1.

title: Explainable Online Lane Change Predictions on a Digital Twin with a Layer Normalized LSTM and Layer-wise Relevance Propagation - Advances and Trends in Artificial Intelligence. Theory and Practices in Artificial Intelligence: 35th International Conference on Industrial, E...
justification: Digital Twin is central (live data from a highway digital twin) and the study explicitly focuses on explainability (LRP for LSTMs) with a human-facing interface for communicating explanations. Satisfies IC1 and IC2.

title: Explainable Human-in-the-Loop Dynamic Data-Driven Digital Twins
justification: Clearly meets Phase 1 criteria: Digital Twins are central (human-in-the-loop DDDAS/DT systems) and the work explicitly focuses on explainability and human interaction (interpretable ML, goal modeling, trustworthiness, trade-off analysis). Peer-reviewed LNCS chapter with English abstract; not a secondary study.

title: An Interpretable Digital Twin for Self-Aware Industrial Machines
justification: Digital Twin is the central focus and the abstract explicitly emphasizes interpretability and transparency. Meets IC1 and IC2; peer-reviewed, English. Clearly relevant for explainable/interpretability aspects in Digital Twins.

title: A Systematic Literature Review of Digital Twin Research for Healthcare Systems: Research Trends, Gaps, and Realization Challenges
justification: The article is a systematic literature review (secondary study) of Digital Twin research in healthcare, which clearly falls under EC3 (secondary studies). While Digital Twins and human-in-the-loop/provider decision-making are discussed, the study type itself is a review, not primary research, and thus should be excluded in Phase 1.

title: TailorAlert: Large Language Model-Based Personalized Alert Generation System for Road Infrastructure Management with Digital Twins
justification: Digital Twin systems are central to the study, and the proposed LLM-based TailorAlert focuses on personalized, user-friendly notifications tailored to roles and expertise, emphasizing human-centered interaction with DTs. This satisfies IC1 and the human interaction aspect of IC2. It is a peer-reviewed conference paper in English and not solely about predictive/simulation models.

title: An Efficient and Effective Cloud Monitoring Architecture based on Data Visualization and Digital Twin Technology
justification: Digital Twin is a central component (interactive digital twin for the cloud platform) and the abstract explicitly addresses interpretability and data visualization, with human interaction implied via an interactive system and user studies. This satisfies IC1 and IC2. No clear exclusion criteria apply.

title: Empowering operators with a human-in-the-loop/on-the-loop simulation-based digital twin: the case of a smart learning factory
justification: Digital Twin is central (simulation-based DT supporting a DSS) and the study focuses on human-centered aspects (human-in/on-the-loop, interactive human-machine interface, operator decision support, comprehension). This satisfies IC1 and IC2. No clear exclusion applies.

title: Device Digital Twin Construction Based on Random Matrix Theory and Deep Auto-Encoder Networks
justification: Digital Twin is central (device-level DT construction for power systems). The study includes explainability/human-centered aspects by providing interpretable visualizations and 3D visualizations to support decision-making, satisfying IC1 and IC2. Peer-reviewed conference paper in English; no clear exclusion applies.

title: Automatically Learning Hybrid Digital Twins of Dynamical Systems
justification: Digital Twins are central, but the work focuses on automatic learning of hybrid DT models to improve prediction, generalization, and sample efficiency. The abstract contains no mention of explainability, interpretability, transparency, or human-centered/interaction aspects. Thus, it fits EC2 (DT modeling without XAI/human aspects) and can be excluded in Phase 1.

title: Delving into the Digital Twin Developments and Applications in the Construction Industry: A PRISMA Approach
justification: The article is a PRISMA-based systematic review (secondary study) on Digital Twin developments in construction, which meets EC3 for exclusion in Phase 1. While DT is central and human-related aspects are mentioned, the study is not a primary research contribution.

title: From Digital Twins to Digital Selves and Beyond - Perspectives for Social Modelling in a Trans-Humanist World
justification: Digital Twins are presented as central baseline representations in cyber-physical systems, and the work explicitly discusses transparency and explainability (a 'transparent and explainable knowledge base') along with human/social interaction aspects via Digital Selves. It is a peer-reviewed English article, thus meeting IC1 and IC2.

title: ENIGMA: An explainable digital twin security solution for cyber–physical systems
justification: Digital Twins are the central focus, and the work explicitly addresses explainability (XAI, SHAP) and human interaction (security analysts, human–AI gameplay). It clearly satisfies IC1 and IC2 for Phase 1.

title: Exploring digital twins: Attributes, challenges and risks
justification: Central focus on Digital Twins (IC1) and explicitly addresses explainability-related aspects—transparency and interpretability—as key challenges (IC2). Not clearly a secondary study or non-peer-reviewed per EC3, and clearly not exclusively predictive/simulation. Meets Phase 1 inclusion; include for high-recall screening.

title: A discussion about the qualification of digital twins for maintenance models
justification: Digital Twins are central to the work (qualification and evaluation for maintenance models), and the abstract explicitly addresses interpretability, credibility, and trustworthiness of DTs. This satisfies IC1 and IC2; none of the exclusion criteria clearly apply.

title: Big Data in Earth system science and progress towards a digital twin
justification: Although Digital Twins are central and interpretability/human-system aspects are mentioned (meets IC1 and IC2), the article is a review (secondary study) in Nature Reviews Earth and Environment, which clearly falls under EC3 and is excluded in Phase 1.

title: Feasibility of Digital Twins to Manage the Operational Risks in the Production of a Ready-Mix Concrete Plant
justification: Digital Twin is the central focus (DT system for RMC risk management), and the abstract explicitly mentions interpretable predictive maintenance insights and an advanced analytical dashboard for decision support, satisfying IC1 and IC2. It is a peer-reviewed journal article in English and not a secondary study, so no exclusion criteria apply.

title: Digital Twin – Integrated Geomonitoring
justification: Digital Twin is central to the described geomonitoring project (IC1), and the abstract explicitly mentions transparency in presenting results and understanding processes, along with human-in-the-loop elements (mobile GIS, drone validation) (IC2). No clear exclusion criterion applies.

title: Literature Research on the Use and Requirements of Datagram Communication and Protocols in AAS and Digital Twins
justification: The paper is explicitly a literature research/survey on communication protocols for Digital Twins and the Asset Administration Shell, i.e., a secondary study. Per EC3, secondary studies (e.g., surveys) are excluded in Phase 1. While Digital Twins are central and interpretability is mentioned, the clear secondary nature warrants exclusion.

title: CONCEPTUAL ARCHITECTURE OF DIGITAL TWIN WITH HUMAN-IN-THE-LOOP -BASED SMART MANUFACTURING
justification: Digital Twin is the central focus (conceptual architecture for DT in smart manufacturing) and the paper explicitly addresses human-centered interaction (human-in-the-loop, collaborative decision-making, immersive environments for customers and stakeholders). This meets IC1 and IC2(b). No clear exclusion criteria apply.

title: Enhancing Digital Twins with Advances in Simulation and Artificial Intelligence: Opportunities and Challenges
justification: Digital Twins are a central focus and the abstract explicitly mentions trustworthy and explainable AI in conjunction with Digital Twins and simulation. This satisfies IC1 and IC2. It is a peer-reviewed conference proceeding, so no clear exclusion applies.

title: A General Framework for Human-in-the-Loop Cognitive Digital Twins
justification: Digital Twins are central (cognitive digital twin framework) and the abstract explicitly emphasizes explainability and human-in-the-loop aspects. This satisfies IC1 and IC2, and none of the exclusion criteria apply.

title: Toward Digital Twins for Human-in-the-loop Systems: A Framework for Workload Management and Burnout Prevention in Healthcare Systems
justification: Meets IC1: Digital Twin is the central concept (conceptual HITL workload DT for healthcare). Meets IC2 via human-centered/interaction aspects (human-in-the-loop, provider workload, burnout prevention, feedback mechanisms). It is a peer-reviewed conference paper in English and not exclusively about predictive/simulation models. Therefore it clearly satisfies Phase 1 inclusion.

title: Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) Empowered Digital Twin on Soil Carbon Emission Management Using Proximal Sensing
justification: Digital Twin is the central focus (soil carbon emissions DT), and the work explicitly addresses explainability/interpretability and transparent decision-making via XAI in the DT context. It is a peer-reviewed conference paper in English. Meets IC1 and IC2; no clear exclusion applies.

title: The ethics of human digital twins: Counterfeit people, personhood, and the right to privacy
justification: Digital Twins are central (human digital twins) and the article focuses on human-centered aspects (ethics, personhood, privacy, consent). This satisfies IC1 and IC2(b). It is an IEEE conference paper with English title/abstract and is not a secondary study.

title: Uncertainty-aware explainable AI as a foundational paradigm for digital twins
justification: Digital Twins are central to the article, and it explicitly focuses on explainability (UAXAI), uncertainty quantification, transparency, and human-centered trust/stakeholder interaction in the context of Digital Twins. This clearly meets IC1 and IC2, with no exclusion criteria triggered.

title: A digital twin model for evidence-based clinical decision support in multiple myeloma treatment
justification: Digital Twin is central to the proposed clinical decision-support model for multiple myeloma; the abstract explicitly emphasizes explainability, interpretability, and transparency, and addresses trust/ethical considerations. Meets IC1 and IC2 and does not trigger any exclusion criteria.

title: Design of Digital Twin Sensing Strategies Via Predictive Modeling and Interpretable Machine Learning
justification: Digital Twin is central (methodology for sensor placement and scheduling in digital twins), and the study explicitly uses interpretable machine learning (optimal classification trees) to provide explainable structural assessments and inform decisions. Satisfies IC1 and IC2; peer-reviewed journal article.

title: Development of Digital Twin for Intelligent Maintenance of Civil Infrastructure
justification: Digital Twin is the central focus (DT architecture for infrastructure maintenance), and the abstract explicitly references interpretability (‘more expressible and interpretable’), visualization for decision-making, and human-centered maintenance decision support. This satisfies IC1 and IC2. No exclusion criteria are met.

title: An Outlook of Digital Twins in Offensive Military Cyber Operations
justification: Clearly meets IC1 and IC2: Digital Twins are central to the paper’s framework for offensive military cyber operations, and it explicitly embeds explainable AI/responsible AI perspectives. It appears to be a peer-reviewed conference paper with an English abstract. No clear EC violations.

title: A digital-twin based worker's work allocation framework for a collaborative assembly system
justification: Digital Twin is central to the proposed framework (assembly line digital twin for worker–cobot allocation). The abstract explicitly mentions human-in-the-loop decision-making, satisfying the human interaction aspect. Therefore, it meets IC1 and IC2 and should be included in Phase 1.

title: Explainable Online Lane Change Predictions on a Digital Twin with a Layer Normalized LSTM and Layer-wise Relevance Propagation
justification: Digital Twin is central (live data from a highway digital twin) and the work focuses on explainability (LRP for explaining LSTM predictions) with a human-facing interface. Clearly meets IC1 and IC2; peer-reviewed LNCS chapter with English title/abstract. No exclusion criteria apply.

title: A performance prediction method for a high-precision servo valve supported by digital twin assembly-commissioning
justification: Digital Twin is central (digital twin assembly-commissioning system), and the abstract explicitly mentions interpretability via an information entropy-based feature selection method. This satisfies IC1 and IC2. It is a peer-reviewed article with an English abstract, and not exclusively focused on prediction without explainability or human aspects.

title: Digital twin, physics-based model, and machine learning applied to damage detection in structures
justification: Digital Twin is a central focus (framework and construction for damage detection), satisfying IC1. The abstract explicitly mentions an 'interpretable model (physics-based)' integrated with machine learning, which relates to explainability/interpretability, satisfying IC2. It is a peer-reviewed English article, and does not fall under exclusions.

title: Digital twin-driven human-centered design frameworks for meeting sustainability objectives
justification: Digital Twin is central (DT-driven design, D-HIL methodology), and the work emphasizes human-centered/interaction aspects (human-in-the-loop, HFE, ergonomics decision-making, human error reasoning). Meets IC1 and IC2(b). No clear exclusion criteria apply.

title: Enhancing Human-in-the-Loop Adaptive Systems through Digital Twins and VR Interfaces
justification: Digital Twin is a central concept for representing the adaptive system and its context, and the article explicitly addresses human-in-the-loop aspects, transparency, and interaction via VR interfaces. This satisfies IC1 and IC2; no clear exclusion criteria apply.

title: Explainable Modeling in Digital Twin
justification: The article centrally addresses Digital Twins and proposes a framework for explainable modeling within DTs, explicitly focusing on explanations, understandability, trust, and stakeholder collaboration/interaction. This satisfies IC1 and IC2. It is a peer-reviewed conference proceeding in English and does not solely focus on predictive/simulation models without human or explainability aspects.

title: Robotics, digital twins and AI: Connecting the dot matrix
justification: The paper presents a digital architecture that explicitly optimizes both robot and digital twin capability, making Digital Twins a relevant concept (IC1). It also discusses explainability-related aspects, citing the need for fully explainable, transparent, verifiable autonomy, and touches on human-centered remote operation (IC2). It is a conference paper with an English abstract and not clearly a short/poster/tutorial. Therefore, it meets Phase 1 inclusion criteria.

title: Lightweight Hybrid Deep Learning Model with Digital Twin for Industrial Energy Optimization
justification: Digital Twin is clearly central (IC1) based on the title. However, the abstract is missing, so it is unclear whether explainability or human-centered aspects (IC2) are addressed. It cannot be confidently excluded under EC2 without further details. Given the high-recall Phase 1, this warrants a 'maybe' for potential relevance.

title: Digital Twin–Enabled Personalized Clinical Trials with Reliable and Explainable Data Pipelines using Organic Synthesis Model
justification: The title indicates Digital Twin is a central concept (“Digital Twin–Enabled Personalized Clinical Trials”) and explicitly mentions explainability (“Explainable Data Pipelines”), satisfying IC1 and IC2. It appears to be a peer-reviewed IEEE conference paper in English. No exclusion criteria are clearly met.

title: Integrating Digital Twins and Machine Learning in Industry 4.0: State of the Art and Research Perspectives
justification: The title indicates a state-of-the-art/research perspectives survey on integrating Digital Twins and Machine Learning, which is a secondary study. Per EC3, secondary studies (e.g., surveys) are excluded. Additionally, there is no clear evidence from the title of explainability or human-centered aspects.

title: Detection and Compliance in Financial Management via 6G-Enabled Standardized AI-Powered Digital Twins
justification: Digital Twins are central per the title (IC1). While the abstract is unavailable and explainability/human interaction is not explicit, the compliance-focused financial management context and standards orientation plausibly involve transparency, auditability, or human oversight (IC2).
